notes.title: Achievement Unlocked: Faster, Harder, all with a controller!
notes.notes: [p]As with all demo releases, if you don’t get it the first time, keep trying. And it paid off because I addressed all the issues the players had:[/p][list][*][p]Maps are now small enough so you won’t feel like you are in a walking simulator, but not as tiny as a 21st-century spaceship.[/p][/*][*][p]Puzzles and key items have a much better description, not making it too easy on players, but not as hard as searching for a guide.[/p][/*][*][p]Controller support existed before, but I am confident it is more in a beta phase, addressing issues with interaction. I am a solo developer, so if you are passionate about controllers on a PC, support the future of Immortum by providing valuable feedback in our community page (even positive feedback counts!). ːsteamthumbsupː[/p][/*][*][p]All the maps were optimized and now run much more smoothly.[/p][/*][/list][p]So what are you waiting for? This is the best time to play the Immortum Demo![/p]

notes.title: Getting lost can be a bad thing
notes.notes: [p]Players resonated with Immortum’s Demo, and it was a pleasure to see the faces of those lost in its depths. However, not all games are perfect, and the demo required some fixes.[/p][p]Keeping the balance between making the game fun to play without changing its core was a challenge. Challenge is a positive word since it brings much-needed change![/p][p]Improvements in the current patch are:[/p][list][*][p]Key cards and items that belong to a certain room will now have that room mentioned in their description.[/p][/*][*][p]Small fixes and tweaks to rooms that were buggy. Now you have a more probable chance of dying.[/p][/*][/list][p]Additionally, the biggest feedback was that the corridors are too long. So buckle up for the next patch, where many of the hallways will be scaled down to a more digestible size without sacrificing gameplay and fun.[/p][p]Regarding the game itself, two of the first levels are already a part of the demo, and will be followed by two more levels, one of which is going strong and close to completion.[/p][p]I’ll see you on the next post, where I’ll share the final details about the demo.[/p]

notes.title: Demo Release Date: July 15th
notes.notes: [p]I have created Immortum out of a passion for Horror games. Drawing inspiration from what I like and creating what I wanted to see led to a game that can stand its own ground in today's Horror game scene.[/p][p]The official demo release date, July 1st, was communicated to enthusiastic content creators willing to try Immortum's Demo before everybody else. The reception was amazing and the dream I once had became a reality.[/p][p]Sadly, beyond development, there is also life happening around me, and being solo, I cannot delegate work to others. I am in the process of moving and creating a better working environment for my Quantomuse studio, and unfortunately, it means that Immortum has to be delayed a little.[/p][p]Therefore, Immortum's demo will be out on the 15th of July. So hold tight, and don't forget to tell your friends to get ready! [/p]

notes.title: Why did play testers get lost? Demo play test updates!
notes.notes:
[p][b]Maps are tricky.[/b]

Immortum started without any maps. As an ever-changing maze of corridors, the player should be on the edge of his seat without knowing what lurks beyond the corner.

But the reality was different than expected and players got lost.

Then how do we keep the tension of not knowing the entire map without getting lost?
It took some time to find the answer.

The first obvious answer is an interactive map. Players won't get lost but they will see the entire map, which defeats the purpose of mystery. And honestly, it's a big feature to build that would take focus from the rest of the game.

If not an interactive map, then [b]a static map would be better[/b]. And that's when the solution of a map per corridor came to mind. When you enter or exit a corridor you are presented with a map showing the rooms available to you.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45477220/885fec0bd5b5828ed1268658d64cfe7c2f9eca2b.png"][/img]Each room type has a letter assigned to it. [b]Can you guess what each letter means?[/b] There is a sense to it.
The icons are there to keep the mystery and reduce the amount of translations required in the future. And the design is as simple and straightforward as the Immortum design philosophy.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45477220/3f2f71021c028cb3483db563088328c848a292ab.jpg"][/img]
[b]Navigation wasn't the only thing players got lost in. It was text.[/b]

When playtesters interacted with the NPCs it wasn't clear who was talking.
[b]The solution was a tried and true NPC name that appeared above the text[/b]. But because Romi is the eyes through which you experience the story, if an NPC is a stranger then there will be "???".

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45477220/6485ba61b192a97aca1887d9726fcd9d4db4e403.jpg"][/img]The rest of the changes are some bug fixes and optimizations to make the game run smoother. I plan to release the demo by June's next fest and it looks like we are on track with that. The second phase of closed beta tests will start soon.  So what do you think the letters in the map mean?[/p]
